of: report-format.md § Section 4 · What this change reaches, § Impact paths
notes: The section a diff cannot produce at all, so the eval is mostly about the searching — and, since the reorder, about ROUTING. Section 4 now runs after the behaviour flows, so an affected entry a flow already explained belongs here as a named pointer and nothing more; only code no single flow owns is explained here. That is why whether an entry is RIGHT is graded in cases/behaviour-flows.json, where the explanation lives, and what is graded here is whether the pairing is complete, correctly routed and honestly searched. Presence is mechanical and split across two checks: checks/reach.rb for the section's composition, and checks/impact-paths.rb for the panel — its 2-3 paths, one per card, its three node kinds, its labelled edges and its caps. reach.rb also fails a reading order left in this section: that moved to section 3. Note what the section no longer carries: a Changed list. It used to hold the whole diff, which made it a second ledger a few sections early; the inventory is section 7's at --full and details.coverage-foot's at --brief.

cases.expected_output: An impact-paths panel whose chains run from the new column, through the unchanged query that scopes the selectable list, to what a user would then see, and one affected-but-unchanged list beneath it, the full measure. app/queries/active_projects.rb belongs to Flow B, so it appears as a named pointer to that flow rather than as an explanation. No reading order and no ranking of files: those live in section 3 now. This case is the full level, where section 4 is a section of its own; cases/brief-tail.json is the same material as the default level's merged tail section.
expectations: app/queries/active_projects.rb is in the affected list, and the search that found it is written down

At least one empty search is recorded as a search — an unrecorded absence cannot be told from an omission, and this diff has real ones (no other caller of archive!, no other reader of the archived scope)

Every impact path ends at an observable behaviour rather than at a function, and every one passes through at least one .ip-aff node — a chain that stays inside the diff is a call stack, not an impact path. The edges carry causal verbs and read from the node above to the node below

Routing is right: an entry a flow already explains is a named pointer to that flow — a clause and a link, not the finding again with its citation and tier repeated. Anything explained in full here is genuinely owned by no single flow
It reads as a second pass rather than a first screen: it assumes the flows have been read, and does not re-teach the archival mechanism in order to make its own entries intelligible
The slug uniqueness validation appears as secondary work in a neutral register: independently reviewable, no criticism of the author for bundling it

The recorded searches sit in a collapsed details.searched and the section reads complete with it shut: every finding that rests on an empty result — 'nothing else reads this' — is stated in the open prose, never left for the reader to infer from a row inside the toggle

Each search is one row of a command and a result clause, not a paragraph. A row that re-explains why an entry matters, when the entry sits two inches above it, is the restatement this format forbids arriving as provenance
